Home > Catalog Filtering & Taxonomy > Official Attributes Reference

Official Card Attributes Reference

Every card in the catalog carries official rules attributes synchronized from the Cardnum open database. These keys can be filtered via UI Slots 1 & 2, queried in procedural deck rules, or inspected in the right-click Card Attributes monospace view.

1. Core Identifiers & Metadata

Key Type Example Values Notes
Name string "Wood-elves", "Rivendell", "Glamdring" Exact English card title. Queryable in deck generation rules and cross-card token lookups.
Set string "METW", "MEDM", "MELE", "MEBA" Canonical 4-letter expansion set code.
FullCode string "Wood-elves (TW)", "Adrazar (LE)" Set-disambiguated title used by Cardnum and Play MECCG.
Text string Rules text printed on the face of the card. Evaluated by automated taxonomy regex harvesting.

2. Classification & Alignment

Key Values
Primary Character, Resource, Hazard, Site, Region
Secondary Ally, Faction, Creature, Short-event, Long-event, Permanent-event, Minor Item, Major Item, Greater Item, Gold Ring Item, Special Item
Alignment Hero, Minion, Fallen-wizard, Balrog, Neutral
Unique Unique, Non-unique

3. Character & Creature Statistics

Key Values & Lore Normalization
Race Dúnadan, Dwarf, Elf, Hobbit, Man, Wizard, Orc, Troll, Dragon, etc.
Note: Lore sub-races are canonically normalized to Elf and Dwarf for clean queries.
Subrace Preserves original Tolkien sub-races: Silvan Elf, Noldo Elf, Longbeard Dwarf, etc.
Skill Warrior, Scout, Ranger, Sage, Diplomat. Compound skills (e.g. Warrior/Scout) are indexed individually.
Mind, Direct, Prowess, Body, Corruption, MPs Numeric gameplay stats and victory points.
Home Designated home sites for characters (e.g. "Rivendell", "Bree").

4. Sites & Movement

Key Values
Site Free-hold, Border-hold, Ruins & Lairs, Shadow-hold, Dark-hold, Haven
Region Geographic territory (e.g. Arthedain, Rhudaur, Gorgoroth).
Playable, Hoard, Haven Site item-playability flags and nearest haven designations.

Home > Catalog Filtering & Taxonomy > Custom Taxonomy

Custom Taxonomy & Tag Management

MECCG Deck Builder allows you to classify cards using your own custom classification system (e.g., Archetype → Ring Destruction or Role → Scout Support).

1. Taxonomy Manager (Filter > Manage Custom Tags...)

Open Filter > Manage Custom Tags... to access the central management dialog:

  • Add Categories: Create new classification categories (e.g., Archetype, Hazard Package, Role).
  • Rename Categories or Tags: Rename terms across your taxonomy; all tagged cards are updated automatically.
  • Delete Categories or Tags: Safely remove terms from the database and strip them from tagged cards.

2. Tagging Cards & Multi-Tag Assignment

Cards can hold multiple tags within the same custom category:

  • Assign or Reassign Tag: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [Category] > [Tag]. Currently assigned tags display a checkmark (✓). Clicking a checkmarked tag toggles it off.
  • Author New Tag: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...] to create and assign a new tag in one action without disturbing your filter bar.
  • Granular Removal: The Remove Tag menu displays each assigned tag individually, allowing removal without wiping the category.

3. Saving & Loading Custom Tag Sets

  • Filter > Save Tag Set...: Exports your custom taxonomy and all card assignments to a .json file.
  • Filter > Load Tag Set...: Restores a previously saved custom tag set file.

Home > Procedural Deck Generator > Generator Engine

Procedural Deck Generation Engine

MECCG Deck Builder features an automated generation engine that builds legal, randomized decks from declarative JSON rule templates (via Tools > Generate Deck from Rules... or F5).

Core Generation Mechanics

  • Symmetric Filtering: Rules can query official card attributes (Primary, Race, Skill, Name) and custom user taxonomy tags (Faction Focus, Home Region).
  • Strict Legality & Copy Limits: Automatically enforces game limits: maximum 1 copy for unique cards and maximum 3 copies for non-unique cards across the entire deck.
  • Tiered Variety-First Distribution: To maximize card variety, the engine exhausts all 0-copy (unused) cards before assigning 2nd copies, and all 2-copy cards before assigning 3rd copies.
  • Branching Archetypes (RandomChoice): Author multiple company archetypes or hazard strategies in a single file with weighted random selection and dynamic title overrides.
  • Instant Re-Run (F5): Press F5 (Tools > Re-run Deck Rules) to immediately re-run the last used rules file directly from disk without re-opening file dialogs.

Documentation Topics

  • Deck Rules JSON Schema Reference: Complete technical reference for all rule properties, variables, and tokens.
  • Worked Example: Dynamic Faction Recruitment: Step-by-step tutorial demonstrating variable capture, targeted faction recruiting, and fallbacks.

Home > Deck Building & Formats > Deck Operations

Deck Building Operations

Adding Cards

  • Fastest Method: Switch to your desired deck tab on the right, find the card in the Master List, and double-click it.
  • Drag and Drop: Left-click and drag the card from the Master List onto any visible tab list.
  • Targeted Right-Click: Right-click a card in the Master List, open the Copy submenu, and pick the destination tab (Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, Sites). This automatically switches focus to that tab.

Duplicating Cards

To add another copy of a card already in a deck tab, simply double-click it directly within that tab's list.

Moving Cards Between Tabs

  1. Right-click the card inside any deck tab.
  2. Highlight Move.
  3. Select the destination tab. The card is added to the target tab and removed from the current tab.

Deleting Cards

  • Right-click the card in the deck tab and select Delete.

Deck Tab Context Menu Reference

Menu Item Action
[Card Name Header]Shows card title in the active header color.
CopyDuplicates card to Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, or Sites.
MoveTransfers card to another tab and removes it from current tab.
DeletePermanently removes this copy from the current tab.
Card AttributesDisplays a monospace readout of all official database attributes for this card.
Assigned TagsShows user-defined tags currently assigned to this card.
Assign TagAssigns or reassigns a custom tag (active tag is checkmarked), creates a new tag, or authors a new category and tag.
Remove TagRemoves an assigned custom tag from this card.

Home > Procedural Deck Generator > Rules JSON Schema Reference

Deck Rules JSON Schema Reference

Procedural deck generation templates are declarative JSON files loaded via Tools > Generate Deck from Rules... (or re-run instantly with F5). This reference details all JSON schema elements, properties, data types, default values, and token interpolation rules.

1. Root Object (DeckGenerationRuleSet)

Property Type Default Description
DeckTitle string "Generated Deck" Default title assigned to the deck. Can be dynamically overridden by a branch choice at runtime.
RuleSetType string "SequentialRules" Execution strategy identifier (reserved for future execution engines).
Version string "1.0" Schema version indicator.
Rules array of objects [] An ordered list of DeckGenerationRule objects evaluated sequentially from top to bottom.

2. Rule Object (DeckGenerationRule)

Property Type Default Description
RuleType string "FilterQuery" Rule mode:
  • "FilterQuery": Standard query that samples matching cards.
  • "RandomChoice" (or "Choice" / "OneOf"): Evaluates a weighted random branch from Choices.
Name string "" Descriptive name displayed in generation logs and shortfall notices.
Section string "Resources" Target deck partition: "Pool", "Resources", "Hazards", "Sideboard", or "Sites".
Count integer 1 The exact number of card copies requested by this rule.
SaveAs string "" Captures cards successfully selected by this rule into an in-memory variable (e.g. "Leader" or "Scout"). Subsequent rules can interpolate their attributes or tags using {VariableName.Property}.
Sets array of strings [] Restricts sampling to specific expansion set codes (e.g. ["METW", "MEDM"]). If omitted, defaults to the sets currently checked in the app's Set menu.
Attributes object (key-value) {} Dictionary of official Cardnum rules criteria (e.g. "Primary", "Race", "Skill", "Name"). Supports semicolon OR syntax and variable interpolation.
Tags object (key-value) {} Dictionary of custom user taxonomy criteria (e.g. "Archetype": "Ring Destruction"). Supports semicolon OR syntax and variable interpolation.
Fallback object null A nested DeckGenerationRule executed automatically if this rule fails to fulfill its requested Count (due to missing tags, zero matching candidates, or deck uniqueness limits). Inherits the parent's target Section if unspecified.
Choices array of objects [] Used when RuleType is "RandomChoice". Contains weighted branches.

3. Branch Choice Object (DeckGenerationChoice)

Property Type Default Description
Name string "" Branch label recorded in the execution log (e.g. "Dwarf Company").
DeckTitle string "" Optional deck title override applied if this branch is selected.
Weight integer 1 Relative lottery weight. Selection probability equals $\frac{\text{Weight}}{\sum \text{Weights}}$.
Rules array of objects [] The list of sub-rules executed sequentially if this branch wins the roll.

4. Query & Placeholder Interpolation Rules

A. Semicolon Multi-Value OR Logic

Any string inside Attributes or Tags can contain multiple semicolon-delimited values. A card matches if it satisfies any of the values: 

"Attributes": {
  "Skill": "Warrior; Scout",
  "Secondary": "Major Item; Minor Item"
}

B. Runtime Variable Interpolation (SaveAs → {...})

When a rule captures a card via "SaveAs": "MyVar", downstream rules can dynamically query that card's properties using bracketed tokens:

Token Syntax Target Source Example Resolved Output
{Variable.AttributeName} Official Card Attribute {Leader.Home} "Rivendell"
{Variable.Race} Official Card Attribute {Leader.Race} "Elf"
{Variable.Tag:CategoryName} Custom User Taxonomy Tag {Leader.Tag:Faction Bonus} "Wood-elves; Silvan Elves"
Unmet Dependency Handling: If a token references a tag or property that is absent on the captured card, it resolves to an empty string (""). The rule recognizes that the requirement was not met and adds 0 cards, cleanly handing execution over to the Fallback rule without crashing.

5. Native Save Files (.json) vs. Rule Templates (.json)

Both deck save files and procedural rule sets share the .json extension, but serve distinct roles:

  • Deck Save Files (File > Save / Open): Store an assembled deck instance. Root keys: CurrentDeckTitle, SetList, PoolList, ResourceList, HazardList, SideboardList, and SiteList.
  • Rule Templates (Tools > Generate Deck): Declarative instructions used to generate random decks on demand. Root keys: DeckTitle, RuleSetType, and Rules.

Home > Deck Building & Formats > Export Formats

Multi-Platform Export Formats

Select File > Export to open the export dialog and choose from the supported formats:

Format Extension Target Platform & Usage
Tabletop Simulator .json Generates five JSON deck files (one for each section: _pool.json, _resource.json, _hazard.json, _sideboard.json, _site.json) formatted for Tabletop Simulator's Saved Objects folder with cloud image links.
Play MECCG .play Standard export for the online Play MECCG client. Formats cards with parenthetical subtitle conventions (e.g. Adrazar (TW)) using Windows-1252 ANSI encoding.
Cardnum Deck .cnum Exports deck listings using standard Cardnum code prefixes (e.g. 1 Adrazar (TW)) grouped by deck sections.
Archive Listing .archive A structured analysis format that breaks down your deck by category: Items (Minor, Major, Greater, Ring), Events (Short, Long, Permanent), Allies, Factions, Characters by race, and Sites by type.
Text File .txt A clean, human-readable plain text breakdown of all deck sections with section headers.

Home > Tools & Technical Architecture > Artwork Cache & Downloader

Card Artwork Cache & Downloader

Card Artwork Cache System

The application employs a high-performance two-tier caching architecture:

  1. Memory Cache: An in-memory cache holding up to 10,000 active Bitmaps for instant display when clicking or navigating.
  2. Local Disk Cache: Checks for card images on disk under local set folders (e.g., METW/metw_adrazar.jpg).
    • If found locally, the image loads immediately with zero network latency.
    • If missing, it downloads asynchronously from Cardnum, saves a copy to disk, and loads it into memory.

Batch Image Downloader

To pre-cache card artwork for tournament or offline use:

  1. Enable all sets you want cached in the Set menu.
  2. Reset filters (Ctrl+R) so all cards appear in the Master List.
  3. Select Tools > Download Images.
Background Download: The batch downloader runs asynchronously with real-time progress reported in the window title bar, keeping the application responsive.

Offline Data Fallbacks

  • Cards: Automatically attempts to download the latest card definitions from Cardnum on launch, falling back to local cards-dc.json if offline.
  • Sets: Attempts to download set metadata on launch, falling back to local sets-dc.json if offline.

Home > Welcome & Getting Started > Overview

MECCG Deck Builder

MECCG Deck Builder is a dedicated Windows desktop application designed to build, organize, filter, and export decks for the Middle-earth Collectible Card Game (MECCG) published by Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.), including official expansions and player council Dreamcard sets.

Key Capabilities

  • Live Data Integration: Synchronizes cards and expansion sets from the Cardnum open database, with seamless local offline JSON fallbacks.
  • On-Demand Image Preview & Caching: Displays high-resolution card artwork downloaded on demand and cached locally to conserve bandwidth.
  • Five-Section Deck Partitioning: Organizes cards into standard MECCG deck sections: Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, and Sites.
  • Dual Filtering Engine: Filter the card catalog simultaneously by official Cardnum metadata (race, skills, items, alignments) and customizable user-defined tags.
  • Procedural Deck Generator: Build legal, randomized decks from declarative JSON rule templates with tiered variety-first duplication and branching archetypes.
  • Multi-Platform Exporting: Directly export decks to Tabletop Simulator (TTS), Play MECCG online client, Cardnum list format, structured text archives, or plain text lists.

Quick Start Guide

  1. Select Card Sets: Click Set in the top menu bar to check the expansions you want to browse (defaults to The Wizards).
  2. Filter Cards: Use the dropdown menus at the bottom left to filter by card properties (such as Primary = Character, Race = Dúnadan).
  3. Add Cards to Your Deck:
    • Double-click any card in the Master List to add it to the active tab on the right.
    • Or drag and drop cards directly into any deck tab.
    • Or right-click a card in the Master List and choose Copy > [Target Tab].
  4. Review Title Bar Counters: Watch the window title update dynamically with card counts: MECCG Deck Builder - "DeckName" (Pool/Resources[Characters]/Hazards/Sideboard/Sites).
  5. Save or Export: Choose File > Save to keep your deck in native JSON format, or File > Export to generate files for Tabletop Simulator or Play MECCG.

Home > Welcome & Getting Started > Interface Walkthrough

User Interface Walkthrough

The application interface is divided into four main functional zones:

1. Master Card List (Left Pane)

Displays all cards matching your active expansion sets and filter criteria, sorted alphabetically.

  • Single-Click: Selects the card and loads its artwork into the preview panel.
  • Double-Click: Appends the card to the currently selected deck tab on the right.
  • Right-Click: Opens the master context menu to copy cards, inspect attributes, view tags, or assign custom tags.
  • Drag & Drop: Left-click and drag the card title onto any deck listbox.

2. Card Image Preview (Center Pane)

Displays high-resolution card artwork downloaded on demand from cardnum.net and cached locally in set folders (e.g., METW/, MEDM/).

Errata Notice: Cards flagged with ICE errata automatically load their corrected image counterpart prefixed with ice-.

3. Deck Tabs (Right Pane)

Five tabbed lists representing standard MECCG deck partitions:

Tab Name Description
PoolStarting PoolCharacters, starting items, and starter resources.
ResResourcesResource events, allies, factions, and playable items.
HazHazardsCreatures, hazard events, and corruption cards.
SideSideboardReserve cards accessible during the game.
SiteSitesSite cards and movement region paths.

4. Filter Bar (Bottom Panel)

Organized into two titled GroupBoxes providing context-sensitive faceted filtering:

  • Left Box — Card Attributes (Official Database): Slots 1 & 2 query official Cardnum rules properties (Attribute above Value).
  • Right Box — Custom Tags (User Taxonomy): Slots 3 & 4 query your custom classification taxonomy (Category above Tag).

Dynamic Title Bar Summary

The window title updates automatically to reflect live deck statistics:

MECCG Deck Builder - "[Deck Title]" (Pool/Res[Characters]/Haz/Side/Site)

For example: MECCG Deck Builder - "Ring Hunter" (5/30[4]/30/20/12) indicates 5 pool cards, 30 resource cards (including 4 characters), 30 hazards, 20 sideboard cards, and 12 sites.

Home > Deck Building & Formats > Saving Native Decks

Saving Native Decks (.json)

Native Save Files (.json)

Use File > Save (Ctrl+S) or File > Open (Ctrl+O) to store and load complete deck configurations in native JSON format.

What is Preserved

  • Deck Title: Derived from the saved file name or procedural template title.
  • Active Expansion Sets: The exact selection of sets used when building the deck.
  • Section Contents: The complete card contents across all 5 deck partitions (Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, Sites).

Save File JSON Structure

Native deck save files store an assembled deck instance using simple card records [Name, ImageName, Set, Id]: 

{
  "CurrentDeckTitle": "Ring Hunter",
  "SetList": [ "METW", "MEDM" ],
  "PoolList": [
    [ "Adrazar", "metw_adrazar.jpg", "METW", "0" ]
  ],
  "ResourceList": [],
  "HazardList": [],
  "SideboardList": [],
  "SiteList": []
}
Rule Templates vs. Save Files: Native deck files represent saved decks. If you want to author generative rule files that create randomized decks from queries, see Deck Rules JSON Schema Reference.

Home > Catalog Filtering & Taxonomy > Sets & Faceted Filtering

Sets & Faceted Filtering

Managing Expansion Sets

Click the Set menu in the top bar to choose which expansions are active in the Master List:

  • Select All: Enables all official sets and Dreamcard expansions.
  • Clear All: Deselects all expansions.
  • Individual Sets: Check or uncheck individual expansions (e.g., The Wizards, The Dragons, Dark Minions, The Lidless Eye, The Balrog, or Dreamcard sets).

Dual-Layer Filtering Architecture

Located beneath the main workspace, four vertical column pairs of ComboBoxes provide fine-grained catalog search:

Filter GroupBox Data Source Behavior
Left GroupBox:
Card Attributes (Official Database)
(Slots 1 & 2)		 Cardnum Database: Canonical rules statistics (Primary, Alignment, Race, Skill, Mind, Prowess). Fixed, read-only rules attributes. See Official Attributes Reference.
Right GroupBox:
Custom Tags (User Taxonomy)
(Slots 3 & 4)		 User Taxonomy: Custom categories and tags managed locally. Editable classification categories. See Custom Taxonomy & Tag Management.

Cascading Faceted Search & Conflict Resolution

  • Context-Sensitive Value Pruning: Every dropdown automatically prunes options to show only values present among cards satisfying your active expansion sets and other active filter slots, completely eliminating zero-result queries.
  • Order-Independent Narrowing: Filters can be selected in any sequence. Selecting Skill = Diplomat in Slot 2 prunes Slot 1's Secondary dropdown down to card types featuring diplomats.
  • Automatic Conflict Resolution: If an active selection becomes impossible (e.g., deselecting an expansion set), the invalid slot automatically resets to blank ("").

Clearing and Resetting Filters

Method Shortcut / Gesture Behavior
Global Reset Filter > Clear All Filters / Ctrl+R Resets all 4 filter slots to blank instantly.
Slot Context Menu Right-Click any filter ComboBox Provides options to clear that specific slot or clear all slots.
Quick Keyboard Reset Escape Resets focused filter ComboBox to blank ("").

Home > Catalog Filtering & Taxonomy > CSV Pipeline

CSV Spreadsheet Pipeline

To facilitate large-scale taxonomy authoring or collaborative review in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel, MECCG Deck Builder supports round-trip CSV draft exporting and importing via the Tools menu.

Spreadsheet Column Layout

Column Header Required? Description & Behavior
Card NameRequiredExact card title (e.g. Anborn, Adrazar). Matches cards in catalog.
SetRequiredExpansion code (e.g. METW, MEDM) used to disambiguate reprint cards.
PrimaryOptionalOfficial primary type (e.g. Character). Read-only; ignored during import.
[Custom Category Columns]OptionalAny header (e.g. Faction Focus, Role) becomes a custom category. Cell contents are imported as tags.
Card TextOptionalFull rules text provided for reference during editing. Ignored during import.
Multi-Tagging Syntax: To assign multiple tags within the same category to a card, separate them with a semicolon (;), for example: Dwarf Factions; All Factions or Scout Support; Ranger Buffer.

Step-by-Step Workflow

  1. Scope the Master List: Select your desired expansion sets and set filter criteria so that only target cards appear in the Master List.
  2. Export Draft: Select Tools > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)....
  3. Edit in Excel / Google Sheets: Add custom category headers, enter tags into cells, and download as a CSV file.
  4. Import to Deck Builder: Select Tools > Import Taxonomy from CSV.... Categories and tags immediately populate filter dropdowns and card context menus.

Home > Tools & Technical Architecture > Taxonomy Extraction Tools

Taxonomy Extraction Tools

Located under Tools > Extract Taxonomy with Rules..., this dialog provides automated classification tools scoped strictly to cards currently visible in your Master List.

1. Dynamic Entity Harvesting (from Catalog Text)

  • Entity Harvest: Select any canonical card rules attribute and value (e.g. Secondary = Faction or Primary = Region). The app automatically scans active sets in memory, extracts all matching entity titles, and searches your scoped Master List cards for references to those entities.
  • Flavor Text Protection: All Tolkien book quotes and citations (enclosed in quotation marks) are automatically stripped before rules evaluation, preventing lore text from creating false-positive tags.

2. Relational Attribute Lookup (Cross-Card Join)

Enables 2-step relational tagging between linked entities:

  • Source Field: Reads an attribute from cards in scope (e.g. Character Home).
  • Lookup Entity: Matches corresponding cards in the catalog (e.g. Primary = Site).
  • Extract Field: Reads the destination attribute (e.g. Site Region) and writes it into a custom category (e.g. Home Region).
  • Compound Token Parsing: Characters with multiple homesites (e.g. Rivendell, Bree) automatically resolve both sites to generate semicolon-delimited multi-tags (Arthedain; Rhudaur).

3. Custom Regex & JSON Rule Files

Test individual regular expressions in real-time or load batch rule sets from portable .json rule files.

Home > Procedural Deck Generator > Worked Example: Dynamic Factions

Worked Example: Dynamic Faction Recruitment

This end-to-end tutorial demonstrates how several advanced features of MECCG Deck Builder work together to solve a complex deck construction problem:

1. The Goal: Context-Aware Deck Archetypes

In MECCG, leaders often possess direct influence (DI) bonuses against specific factions (for example, Thranduil receives +2 DI against the Wood-elves, and Dáin II receives +2 DI against the Iron Hill Dwarves).

We want to create an automated deck generator rule set that:

  1. Randomly selects a company archetype (e.g. Dwarf Company vs. Elf Company).
  2. Selects an appropriate starting diplomat leader for that company and captures them in memory.
  3. Dynamically recruits the specific faction our leader specializes in influencing.
  4. Gracefully falls back: If the randomly chosen leader has no faction influence bonus, the generator must automatically fall back to recruiting any faction matching that leader's race.

2. Step 1: Scoping the Master List & Auto-Tagging Faction Bonuses

The extraction engine operates strictly on the cards currently visible in the Master List. The cards in this list are determined by two factors:

  • Active Expansions: Checked sets in the top Set menu.
  • Active Filters: The four filter slot pairs at the bottom of the window.

Since we only want to evaluate and tag characters for direct influence bonuses, we narrow the Master List before opening the tool:

A. Scope the Master List to Characters

  1. Click Set in the top menu and ensure your desired expansions are checked (e.g. The Wizards, The Dragons, Dark Minions).
  2. In Filter Slot 1 (bottom left):
    • Set the top dropdown (Attribute) to Primary.
    • Set the bottom dropdown (Value) to Character.
  3. Leave Slots 2, 3, and 4 blank (or press Ctrl+R before setting Slot 1). The Master List now displays only characters from your selected sets.

B. Run the Dynamic Entity Harvest

  1. Open Tools > Extract Taxonomy with Rules....
  2. Note the dialog title and scope hint banner confirming: "Scanning [X] card(s) currently visible in the Master List."
  3. Select the Dynamic Entity Harvest (from Catalog Text) radio button.
  4. Configure the extraction fields:
    • Target Category: Enter Faction Bonus.
    • Attribute: Select Secondary.
    • Value: Select Faction.
  5. Click Test / Preview Matches. The engine performs a two-step query:
    • It scans all active catalog sets in memory to harvest published faction titles (e.g. Wood-elves, Iron Hill Dwarves, Riders of Rohan).
    • It strips all Tolkien flavor quotes from your scoped characters' rules text and flags every character whose active gameplay rules reference one of those factions (e.g. "+2 direct influence against Wood-elves").
  6. Click Apply Tags to Catalog. Your characters are now permanently assigned structured tags in your session taxonomy (e.g. Thranduil → Faction Bonus: Wood-elves, Dáin II → Faction Bonus: Iron Hill Dwarves).
Faceted Filter Verification: Once applied, you can immediately test these tags in the main window: reset Slot 1, select Category = Faction Bonus in Slot 3, and watch the Tag dropdown populate with all harvested factions!

3. Key Generation Concepts Explained

A. Archetype Branching (RandomChoice)

The RandomChoice rule type rolls weighted random branches at runtime. Each branch can define its own unique sub-rules and automatically update the deck title (e.g., "Hero Elves of the Woodland Realm").

B. Runtime Variable Capture (SaveAs)

Adding "SaveAs": "Leader" to a rule captures whichever character is randomly sampled into a temporary execution context. Subsequent rules can reference that card's properties using {Leader.Attribute} or {Leader.Tag:Category}.

C. Direct Card Title Access (Name)

In the application interface, the filter dropdowns and context menus list official game rules statistics (such as Race, Skill, Mind, Direct). However, inside the rules engine, Name is a fully queryable attribute. Querying "Name": "{Leader.Tag:Faction Bonus}" matches the faction card whose title equals the leader's tagged bonus.

D. Token Interpolation & Multi-Value OR Matching

If a character possesses bonuses for multiple factions (e.g. Wood-elves; Silvan Elves), the token resolves to a semicolon-delimited string. The engine automatically evaluates this as an OR query, matching either faction.

E. Automated Shortfall Fallbacks (Fallback)

If the leader has no faction bonus tag, or if that faction is unique and already at its deck limit, the primary rule experiences a shortfall (0 of 1 added). Instead of halting or leaving an incomplete deck, the engine detects the shortfall and immediately executes the nested Fallback rule for the remaining count.

4. Step 2: The Complete Rule Set (JSON)

Save the following JSON into a file named Hero_Faction_Rules.json:

  "DeckTitle": "Hero Faction Theme Deck",
  "RuleSetType": "SequentialRules",
  "Version": "1.0",
  "Rules": [
    {
      "RuleType": "RandomChoice",
      "Name": "Starting Company Archetype",
      "Choices": [
        {
          "Name": "Dwarf Company",
          "DeckTitle": "Hero Dwarves of the Iron Hills",
          "Weight": 1,
          "Rules": [
            {
              "Name": "Starting Dwarf Leader",
              "SaveAs": "Leader",
              "Section": "Pool",
              "Count": 1,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Character",
                "Race": "Dwarf",
                "Skill": "Diplomat; Warrior"
              }
            },
            {
              "Name": "Dwarf Company Members",
              "Section": "Pool",
              "Count": 4,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Character",
                "Race": "Dwarf"
              }
            },
            {
              "Name": "Leader's Associated Faction",
              "Section": "Resources",
              "Count": 1,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Resource",
                "Secondary": "Faction",
                "Name": "{Leader.Tag:Faction Bonus}"
              },
              "Fallback": {
                "Name": "Fallback Dwarf Faction",
                "Attributes": {
                  "Primary": "Resource",
                  "Secondary": "Faction",
                  "Race": "{Leader.Race}"
                }
              }
            },
            {
              "Name": "Secondary Dwarf Faction",
              "Section": "Resources",
              "Count": 1,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Resource",
                "Secondary": "Faction",
                "Race": "Dwarf"
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "Name": "Elf Company",
          "DeckTitle": "Hero Elves of the Woodland Realm",
          "Weight": 1,
          "Rules": [
            {
              "Name": "Starting Elf Leader",
              "SaveAs": "Leader",
              "Section": "Pool",
              "Count": 1,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Character",
                "Race": "Elf",
                "Skill": "Sage; Diplomat"
              }
            },
            {
              "Name": "Elf Company Members",
              "Section": "Pool",
              "Count": 4,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Character",
                "Race": "Elf"
              }
            },
            {
              "Name": "Leader's Associated Faction",
              "Section": "Resources",
              "Count": 1,
              "Attributes": {
                "Primary": "Resource",
                "Secondary": "Faction",
                "Name": "{Leader.Tag:Faction Bonus}"
              },
              "Fallback": {
                "Name": "Fallback Elf Faction",
                "Attributes": {
                  "Primary": "Resource",
                  "Secondary": "Faction",
                  "Race": "{Leader.Race}"

# Coding Standards & Guidelines: MECCG Deck Builder
## 1. General Principles - Modern .NET Standard: Target C# 12 / .NET 8 idioms (collection expressions [], pattern matching, nullability annotations). - Separation of Concerns: Keep UI presentation (Form1.cs) strictly separated from domain logic, file I/O, network access, and deck generation algorithms. Forms should act as views, delegating logic to dedicated services or models. - Fail-Safe & User-Friendly: Catch exceptions gracefully, report actionable messages to the user, and never let unhandled background exceptions crash the UI thread.
---
## 2. Naming Conventions
### Identifiers - Classes, Records, Enums, Structs, Methods, Properties: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardCatalog, GenerateDeck(), DeckTitle - Local Variables, Method Parameters, Private Fields: Use camelCase. - Examples: cardIndex, selectedSet, filePath - Private / Internal Class Fields: Prefix with an underscore _ or use standard camelCase. - Examples: _cards, _httpClient (or cards, s_httpClient for static instances). - Constants: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardnumCardsUrl, PoolFileSuffix (avoid ALL_CAPS). - Event Handlers in WinForms: Use ControlName_EventName in PascalCase. - Examples: ContentsToolStripMenuItem_Click, ListBoxMaster_SelectedIndexChanged - Note: Ensure the control name starts with an uppercase letter to satisfy Roslyn rule IDE1006.
---
## 3. Architecture & Domain Modeling
### Strongly-Typed Models over Raw Arrays - No More string[] for Entities: Replace List<string[]> and SortedDictionary<string, string> with strongly-typed records or classes (e.g., Card, DeckCard, DeckSection). - Enums for Domain Constants: Use strongly-typed enums for fixed concepts (e.g., DeckSection.Pool, DeckSection.Resources, CardAlignment.Hero). - Immutability Where Appropriate: Card catalog definitions should be read-only once loaded into memory.
### Headless & Testable Domain Logic - Deck export routines, deck import routines, card filtering, and the future procedural deck generator must never take ListBox, ComboBox, or Form controls as parameters. - Operate on pure domain structures (e.g., Deck, IEnumerable<Card>, FilterCriteria) so they can be tested via unit tests and run headless.
---
## 4. Asynchronous Programming & Threading
### No Blocking on Async Tasks - Never use .Result, .Wait(), or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on the UI thread. - All network requests (HttpClient) and disk I/O should use async / await: - Avoid: string json = s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url).Result; - Prefer: string json = await s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url); - Long-running batch operations (such as Download Images or Generate Deck) must be performed asynchronously or on a background task (Task.Run) with progress updates via IProgress<T> or Progress<int>.
---
## 5. Resource Management & GDI+ Safety
### Safe Image Loading (No File Locking) - Never instantiate new Bitmap(filePath) directly for files that might be overwritten or deleted, as GDI+ keeps the file locked indefinitely. - Instead, read the image bytes into a MemoryStream and create an independent Bitmap clone: - Read bytes via File.ReadAllBytes(filePath) - Copy into MemoryStream - Construct Bitmap from stream and return an independent instance.
### Disposal of GDI+ Objects - When assigning a new image to PictureBox.Image, always dispose of the previous image if it is an unmanaged, uncached copy to prevent GDI object leaks. - Always dispose Graphics, Pen, Brush, and Font objects using using statements.
---
## 6. Encodings & String Formats
- Internal Strings: Standard .NET UTF-16 strings. - JSON Serialization: Use UTF-8 without BOM (System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json). - Legacy Play MECCG Files (.play): Explicitly specify Windows-1252 ANSI: - Encoding.GetEncoding(1252) - HTML Help Files (.hhp, .hhc, .hhk): Must be saved as ANSI (Windows-1252) or UTF-8 without BOM/signature. Never save help project files with a UTF-8 BOM.
---
## 7. Error Handling & Defensive Coding
- No Silent Exception Swallowing: Avoid empty catch (Exception) { } blocks. At minimum, log the error or provide user feedback via a status bar or message box. - Specific Exception Catching: Catch specific exceptions (e.g., HttpRequestException, JsonException, IOException) before general Exception. - Collection Key Safety: Use TryGetValue() or ContainsKey() before accessing dictionaries to prevent KeyNotFoundException.
---
## 8. Formatting & Tooling - Indentation: 4 spaces (no tabs in C# source files; tabs permitted only in generated export templates if required by format specification like Tabletop Simulator JSON). - Line Endings: CRLF (\r\n) for Windows compatibility. - Warnings as Errors: Aim for zero compiler warnings and zero Roslyn analyzer warnings on Release builds.

# MECCG Deck Builder
An offline-capable Windows desktop application for building, organizing, filtering, and exporting decks for the **Middle-earth Collectible Card Game (MECCG)** by Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.), including official expansions and Council of Elrond Dreamcard sets.
---
## Features
- **Complete Card Database:** Automatically synchronizes card and set definitions from the open Cardnum database, with offline local JSON fallback. - **Five-Section Deck Partitions:** Manage cards across standard competitive partitions: - **Pool:** Starting company, starter items, and opening resources. - **Resources:** Resource events, allies, factions, and items. - **Hazards:** Creatures, hazard events, and corruption. - **Sideboard:** Sideboard reserves. - **Sites:** Sites and movement regions. - **Dynamic Stats Summary:** Window title bar displays live card counts per section with dedicated character counts: `(Pool / Res [Characters] / Haz / Side / Site)`. - **Card Artwork Preview & Caching:** On-demand card artwork download from Cardnum with local disk caching (`METW/`, `MEDM/`, etc.) and an in-memory cache. ICE errata cards load corrected artwork automatically. - **Dual-Layer Filtering:** - **Official Card Attributes (Slots 1 & 2):** Filter by Primary type, Alignment, Race, Skills, Stats, Unique status, Sites, and more. - **Custom User Taxonomy (Slots 3 & 4):** Filter by custom categories and tags (e.g., `Archetype` -> `Ring Destruction`, `Role` -> `Scout Support`). Author tags via the dedicated **Manage Custom Tags** dialog or right-click **Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...]** without disturbing active filter criteria. - **Multi-Platform Export Formats:** - **Tabletop Simulator (`.json`):** Generates ready-to-use deck files compatible with TTS MECCG mods. - **Play MECCG (`.play` & `.playPBEM`):** Native format for online play. - **Cardnum Deck (`.cnum`):** Standard `1 <Code>` listing format. - **Archive Breakdown (`.archive`):** Categorized breakdown (Items, Events, Characters by race, Sites by type). - **Plain Text (`.txt`):** Formatted deck listing. - **Procedural Deck Generator:** Generate complete decks from JSON rule files with attribute/tag queries, copy limits, tiered variety-first duplication, and random branching choices (`RandomChoice`). Features runtime variable capture (`SaveAs`), dynamic cross-card token queries (e.g. `{Leader.Tag:Faction Bonus}`, `{Leader.Home}`), and automated shortfall fallbacks (`Fallback`). Re-run instant variations with <kbd>F5</kbd>. - **Relational Taxonomy Extraction:** Cross-reference card attributes across entities (such as mapping Character `Home` to Site `Region`) to produce automatic multi-tags.
---
